sentences.text: The claimant is in appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.
2. The occurrence of the accident and the liability of the Insurer to satisfy the compensation is not in dispute.
3. The Tribunal, on consideration of evidence, proceeded to award a sum of Rs.3,26,759/- as compensation.

4. It is the contention of the claimant that the Tribunal has erred in not awarding any sums towards loss of future income after recording a finding that the claimant has in fact suffered permanent residual disability at 15% to the whole body and the sums awarded under other heads were on the lower side.

5. In my view, having regard to the fact that the Doctor has assessed the permanent residual disability at 15% to the whole body and having regard to the further deposition that the claimant could do his job sitting at one place, it would be appropriate to assess the disability at 10% to the whole body.
6. The fact that the claimant was gainfully employed stands established by filing of his IT returns which indicates that he had an income of Rs.8,67,189/- per annum after deduction of tax.
The Tribunal has accepted the same and assessed the income of the claimant at Rs.72,265/- per month.
This assessment of the Tribunal being based on documentary evidence cannot be found fault with.

7. The claimant being aged 67 years, the multiplier to be adopted would be '5'.
8.

As a consequence, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.4,33,590/- (Rs.72,265/- X 12 X 5 X 10%)
towards loss of future income.

sentences.text: The amount of Rs.40,000/- awarded towards pain and sufferings, Rs.30,000/- awarded towards loss of amenities, food, nourishment, attendant, conveyance charges, Rs.1,44,530/- awarded towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.62,229/- awarded towards medical expenses by the Tribunal, being just and proper, are affirmed.

10. In this appeal, an application was filed by the claimant seeking to produce additional documents i.e., bills for the hip replacement surgery that he had undergone as advised by the Doctor earlier, in respect of which, a sum of Rs.50,000/- has already been awarded by the Tribunal.
The bills produced indicate that the claimant has incurred a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards hip replacement surgery.

11. Learned counsel for the claimant also filed a memo indicating that claimant's son who had earlier been employed in Bosch Company and was entitled to seek for medical coverage of his father was no longer working there and therefore, the claimant had to bear the expenses of the surgery.
12. In view of the above, Rs.5,00,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses as against Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
13. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.12,10,349/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till its realization.
However, the claimant would be entitled to interest on future medical expenses from 14.03.2021 (i.e., the date on which he was hospitalised for hip replacement surgery) till the date of realization.
15. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
16. On such deposit being made, the claimant would be entitled to withdraw the compensation amount.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
